title: Swimlanes and locks: each ticket in one manager's lane, one owner at a time, hand-offs with a note
why: decisions/0180 R2 (rollout item 2; §5 "Every ticket routes to exactly one of the seven middle managers by its domain"; §7 "One owner at a time" and "Sequential hand-offs … with hand-off notes"; #1460: who works what comes from the appendix). The gap 0180 §5 leaves (how a ticket's domain is read, and which lane is which) is filled by who does the work, from the appendix's reporting lines, as reviewed by the session manager (2026-11-26): orders and fulfilment the Customer Service Manager (17 reports there), billing the Accounting Manager (19), an order's payment Customer Service; data, addresses, nations, privacy, the system's own pages and audits the IT Manager (20-25); the marketplace the Sales Director (31, 32); content and design the Editorial Director (26-28); SEO and campaigns the Marketing Director (29, 30); else the Project Manager. Territory still decides the Tier 4 review (§4). One owner per ticket: the existing owner (a person, or one role); a role never takes a person's ticket, and another role's hold lapses after the hour (TeamRunner::mayWork). Hand off to another lane… with a required note, logged, by the lane's manager, an executive above it, or the Founder (Tier 3, §1). Lanes are routing: never in TeamRunner::ruleData, so the decision tree's approval stands (tested: the same fingerprint before and after). Also: live's why column holds 400 characters, so R1's two long tickets kept only their first 400; their full reason goes into goal where it's empty. The before-and-after check is on for this release, as the role-22 fix's proof (#1472). Sent again (Release #317 withdrew itself on staging: "Migrations ran on staging: 2026-11-26_0180_r2_lanes.sql: Integrity constraint violation: 1062 Duplicate entry '59' for key 'PRIMARY'"): staging's counter for control_gauge_tasks sits behind the rows catch-up copied from live, so the seven new tickets now name their own id, one past the highest there, each still added only once. Sent a third time (Release #318 was withdrawn by the before-and-after check at 06:24 UTC: "Doesn't open now: TimeoutError" on /admin/crawler-review.php at 390, as executive and ops-staff; its own checks on staging passed). The shared file this release changes is website/js/tv-ask.js (reach.py: within two steps of 80 of the site's 92 pages); crawler-review.php is reached only through it. The check now tries such a page once more after the look with 90 s, a note if it opens or was slow before too, a block only if it opened before and hangs after (Tier 4 review: CEO, 2026-11-27, Prior Ruling Check yes (0179 rule 2's far-page note, measured)). Nothing in the release changed. Sent a fourth time as r2-lanes-3 on Sync 19:50 UTC (dd02bdd): the before-and-after check's tab fold (#1569) and timed-out before looks (#1598) are fixed and live in Release #324; faq.md's one entry re-applied on the live copy, the other eight files unchanged since 02:50. Sent a fifth time as r2-lanes-4 on Sync 01:51 UTC (b91644e): Release #325 was withdrawn by the before-and-after check on /admin/crawler-review.php at 390 (a page whose width comes and goes with its records, reached only through js/tv-ask.js); the check's gap is closed in #1648. faq.md rebuilt on the live copy (writeOrder's #326 sentence kept); nothing else changed.
data_reason: R1's two long Work tickets (the 6:13 jobs; the before-and-after check's false blocks) lost their reason past 400 characters to live's why column (live read of control_gauge_tasks, 2026-11-26); their full reason is written into goal, a TEXT column, only where goal is empty, so nothing a person wrote is touched.
